transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?
I’ve gotten really slowed down at work. I can sit there staring at an audit workpaper for twenty minutes before I can even move my hand to type. People have started noticing I’m not keeping up.
How long have you been experiencing this slowed-down feeling and trouble keeping up at work?
About seven months, I think. It started around the time my husband stopped working after the downsizing.
Have you ever had a period, lasting several days or more, where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than normal?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed any times like that.
Have you noticed any other physical changes recently, like increased fatigue, weight gain, feeling unusually cold, or dry skin/hair?

Yes—I'm exhausted a lot. Even if I’ve been in bed all night, my body feels like I’ve been working nonstop for days. Something basic like taking a shower or sorting through insurance paperwork can completely wipe me out.
Have you noticed feeling unusually cold or gaining weight without changes in your diet over these past several months?
I haven’t been gaining weight. Actually, I think I’ve lost some—my work skirts are looser. Food’s mostly something I have to make myself eat because I know I should.
Over these past seven months, have you been feeling down, sad, or empty most of the day, or have you lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
Yes. Most days I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest, like the day is already lost before I even get out of bed.
Before these past seven months, have you ever had another period—lasting two weeks or more—where you felt similarly down, low-energy, or lost interest in things?
I’m not sure. I can’t really think of another time that was like this for two weeks or more.
Have you had any thoughts of death, or thoughts of hurting yourself or not wanting to be alive?
I’m not sure. I mean, I’ve been feeling really low, but I don’t know if I’d call it thoughts of death or hurting myself.
Over these past several months, have you been feeling unusually worthless, or blaming yourself excessively for things, even things that aren't really your fault?

Yes. I keep feeling like I’ve already ruined us financially, even though my husband shows me the bank balance and says we’re okay. And at work, my manager says my job isn’t in danger, but I’m convinced the firm is quietly putting together a case against me because I’m incompetent.

latest_inference.note: The patient's fixed, mood-congruent delusional beliefs (certainty of financial ruin despite reassurance, conviction the firm is building a case against her despite explicit denial) indicate psychotic features accompanying the depressive episode, meeting criteria for severe MDD with psychotic features rather than unspecified depression. This also rules out adjustment disorder (F43.21), as the symptom severity, vegetative signs (anorexia, weight loss, psychomotor slowing), and psychotic-level guilt/worthlessness exceed what is expected from a stressor-reactive adjustment disorder.
